Usage:
  cmux vm network <id>                                   Show the machine's outbound policy.
  cmux vm network <id> set --mode <full|allowlist|none> [--dns <on|off>]
  cmux vm network <id> set --policy <json>               Replace the whole policy.
  cmux vm network <id> add-domain <domain>...
  cmux vm network <id> remove-domain <domain>...
  cmux vm network <id> add-range <cidr> [--port <n>] [--protocol <tcp|udp>] [--note <text>]
  cmux vm network <id> remove-range <cidr> [--port <n>] [--protocol <tcp|udp>]
  cmux vm network <id> preset <add|remove> <preset-id>...

Modes: full reaches any public address; allowlist reaches only the listed
domains and ranges; none reaches nothing. cmux's own hosts stay reachable
in every mode. Domains are exact HTTPS host names (no wildcards). A range
with --port and no --protocol means TCP. Open DNS (--dns on) is itself an
outbound channel. Changes apply live to a running machine, with no restart.
`cmux vm network <id>` lists the preset ids. Add --json for the structured result.
vm new: use either --network or --network-policy, not both.
Show or change whether the machine keeps its coding agents up to date; see `cmux vm agent-updates --help`.
Show or change the machine's outbound network policy; see `cmux vm network --help`.
latest keeps coding agents up to date; image (default) keeps the baked versions
